title: Measure shaft end play and fit a split spacer
instruction: 1. Lift the contact indicator. Hold both reference pads against the housing's rear datum and keep the spring probe aligned with the shaft end while moving the shaft gently to both axial stops. Hold steady at each stop; subtract the lower display reading (0.01 mm resolution) from the higher. 2. Select a split spacer: travel 11.71–11.89 mm → blue 8.80 mm; 11.90–12.10 mm → yellow 9.00 mm; 12.11–12.29 mm → red 9.20 mm. Recheck other readings. Target final end play: 2.90–3.10 mm. 3. Move the shaft to its near stop, withdraw the indicator axially and return it to the table. Insert the spacer from above into the housing channel, opening down and tab up. Leave the fixed end stop installed; do not force an oversized spacer. 4. Repeat the referenced two-stop measurement and verify 2.90–3.10 mm travel. With the spacer retained, rotate the shaft at least 60°. 5. Return the indicator to the table, release and withdraw both hands. The spacer must stay seated and the assembly stable for 2 seconds.
context: Use a measured clearance and a service procedure to select a spacer, fit it, and verify both clearance and rotation in a low-load training fixture.
setup: Standard bimanual YAM station. Fixed 140×120 mm housing base with a horizontal 16 mm shaft, 56 mm thrust collar and fixed end stop; three upright selective split spacers in 0.2 mm steps (8.80 mm blue, 9.00 mm yellow, 9.20 mm red) on a parts mat; a handheld spring contact indicator with two reference pads and a remote readout showing 0.01 mm. One fixed starting layout; dimensions, masses and poses are listed in README and the scene builders.
scoring: 0 initially. 0.25: steady referenced readings (within 0.02 mm over 0.25 s) at both initial axial stops, giving travel within 0.10 mm of the 12.00 mm nominal. 0.5: after measuring, a spacer is seated giving 2.90–3.10 mm physical end play (only the 9.00 mm spacer; the 8.80 and 9.20 mm spacers leave 3.20 and 2.80 mm). 0.75: a second referenced measurement verifies 2.90–3.10 mm, agreeing with physical clearance within 0.05 mm. 1.0: additionally rotate the retained shaft through at least 60 degrees, return the indicator, release and remain stable for 2 seconds. Invalid numeric states score 0; loss of the fitted spacer removes fitting/verification credit.
reset_notes: Reset restores the shaft, loose spacers, indicator, robot joints, spring probe and score history; no consumables.
fidelity: Original training fixture. Indicator resolution 0.01 mm, as on a dial indicator. Spacer steps and the end-play window (0.2 mm) are two to four times coarser than real shims (0.05-0.1 mm), limited by the robot-held indicator's repeatability (about 0.04 mm). The 3 mm nominal end play is far larger than in a real gearbox, as the spacer goes in without a lead-in. Rigid geometry sets the fit; a guide joint stands for the bearing, a spring joint drives the probe. Contacts, masses, friction authored.
scores: Scripted demonstration: 1.0; repeat after reset: 1.0. Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta) on the revised task: 0.0 (2,000 steps, seed 0).
